title: Past Tense Composition - Building Complete Stories
description: Practice combining everything: passé composé, imparfait, causal words, spatial prepositions for rich storytelling
can_do: Combine scene-setting, events, reasons, and locations
Tell rich, sophisticated stories in French

concepts.definition: Set the scene, say what happened and give the reason.

examples.fr: Hier, il faisait beau, donc je suis allé au parc.
examples.en: Yesterday it was nice out, so I went to the park.

examples.fr: J'étais content parce que j'avais du temps.
examples.en: I was happy because I had time.

concepts.term: Building a story step by step
concepts.definition: Start with the scene, add an event, then give the reason for the next event.

examples.fr: Il faisait beau quand je suis sorti.
examples.en: It was nice out when I went out.

examples.fr: J'ai décidé d'aller au café parce que j'avais faim.
examples.en: I decided to go to the café because I was hungry.

concepts.definition: Use the imparfait with words for places to paint the picture.

examples.fr: Le café était près de l'école.
examples.en: The café was near the school.

examples.fr: Il y avait beaucoup de gens.
examples.en: There were a lot of people.

examples.fr: Ils étaient assis autour des tables.
examples.en: They were sitting around the tables.

concepts.definition: Words like {donc} and {comme} tie one event to the next.

examples.fr: Comme il faisait beau, je suis sorti.
examples.en: As it was nice out, I went out.

examples.fr: J'ai vu Marie, donc on a parlé.
examples.en: I saw Marie, so we talked.

examples.fr: On est allés au café car on avait faim.
examples.en: We went to the café because we were hungry.

concepts.definition: Put the events in order with {d'abord} and {ensuite}, and say where each one happened.

examples.fr: D'abord, je suis allé au café près de l'école.
examples.en: First I went to the café near the school.

examples.fr: Ensuite, j'ai vu Marie devant le cinéma.
examples.en: Then I saw Marie in front of the cinema.

examples.fr: Après, j'ai joué avec mon chien.
examples.en: After that I played with my dog.

concepts.term: A verb, then {de} or {à}, then a second verb
concepts.definition: Some verbs take a second verb after {de}, like {décider de}. Others take it after {à}, like {commencer à}.

examples.en: I decided to go to the café.
examples.note: the second verb stays in the infinitive

items.text: Hier, il ___ beau ___ je suis sorti
items.gloss: Yesterday, it was nice so I went out

mistakes.feedback: Weather is background! Use imparfait: il faisait (not a fait).
Use '{donc}' for result/consequence! Il faisait beau DONC je suis sorti.

items.text: Je suis allé au café ___ l'école ___ j'avais faim
items.gloss: I went to the café near the school because I was hungry

mistakes.feedback: Close! But '{près de}' (near) is better than 'devant' (in front) here.
The café is NEAR the school, not IN it! Use '{près de}' (near).

items.text: J'___ avec Marie quand tu as appelé
items.gloss: I was talking with Marie when you called

mistakes.feedback: Actually BOTH work! But if thinking of whole conversation as one unit, '{ai parlé}' works. If emphasizing ongoing, 'parlais' is better. Let's accept both!

items.text: ___ il faisait beau, on est allés au parc
items.gloss: Since it was nice, we went to the park

mistakes.feedback: Parce que rarely starts sentences! Use '{Comme}' at the beginning.
Car CANNOT start a sentence! Use '{Comme}' at the beginning.

items.text: Il y ___ beaucoup de gens ___ des tables
items.gloss: There were many people around the tables

mistakes.feedback: Description of scene! Use imparfait: il y avait (not a eu).
People sit AROUND tables, not ON them! Use '{autour de}' (around).
C'était is ALWAYS imparfait for general evaluation! C'était super.
That's present! Use imparfait: c'était (it was).

items.text: J'ai décidé ___ aller au cinéma ___ j'avais du temps
items.gloss: I decided to go to the cinema because I had time

mistakes.feedback: Both work! '{Parce que}' or 'car' are both fine for 'because'.
'{Décider DE}' (not à)! J'ai décidé D'aller (not à aller).

items.text: On ___ au café chaque samedi, mais hier on n'y est pas allé
items.gloss: We used to go to the café every Saturday, but yesterday we didn't go

mistakes.feedback: Chaque samedi = habit! Use imparfait: on allait (we used to go).
That's present! Use imparfait for past habit: on allait.

items.text: Je marchais tranquillement quand soudain j'___ Marie
items.gloss: I was walking peacefully when suddenly I saw Marie

mistakes.feedback: Soudain = sudden event! Use passé composé: j'ai vu (I saw).
That's present! Use passé composé for past event: j'ai vu.

items.gloss: Because I was hungry, I ate

mistakes.feedback: Grâce à is POSITIVE and needs a NOUN! Use '{Parce que}' + clause for hunger.
À cause de needs a NOUN! Use '{Parce que j'avais faim}' (because I was hungry).

items.text: Le livre était ___ la table ___ la cuisine
items.gloss: The book was on the table in the kitchen

mistakes.feedback: Wrong order! The book is ON (sur) the table, IN (dans) the room.
Au-dessus means 'above' (hanging). Use '{sur}' for '{on}' (touching surface).

items.text: Pendant que je ___, on a parlé pendant une heure
items.gloss: While I was there, we talked for an hour

mistakes.feedback: Ongoing state (while there)! Use imparfait: j'étais (I was there).
That's present! Use imparfait for past state: j'étais.

items.text: J'___ mes devoirs ___ j'ai écouté de la musique
items.gloss: I did my homework then I listened to music

mistakes.feedback: Completed homework = specific event! Use passé composé: j'ai fait.
'Car' is for reason! Use '{ensuite}' (then) for sequence.

items.gloss: Thanks to you, I learned French

mistakes.feedback: Parce que needs a CLAUSE! Use '{Grâce à toi}' (thanks to you - NOUN).
Succeeding is POSITIVE! Use '{grâce à}' (not à cause de which is negative/neutral).

items.text: ___ la fête, on est rentrés tard
items.gloss: Because of the party, we got home late

mistakes.feedback: The party is the cause here, not a thanks. Use '{à cause de}'.
Use '{à cause de la fête}' (because of THE PARTY, a noun).

items.text: Il y avait du pain, alors j'en ___.
items.gloss: There was some bread, so I ate some.

mistakes.feedback: Eating the bread is the event, so use the passé composé: {j'en ai mangé}.
